title: Futures foretold (Kern ch. 6)
hook: the great disciples are told their future Buddha names and lands
tomorrow: The long story of a past Buddha (Kern ch. 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the rain on the plants: one rain fell on every plant, and each grew by its own nature. Your line: one rain, many plants.

At a graduation, the names are read out one at a time. Each person waits for theirs. Some are calm. Some are gripping the arm of the chair. And between one name and the next, the people still waiting wonder if theirs is really on the list. Chapter six of the Lotus has that moment in it, except the list is of future Buddhas, and the ones waiting are some of the Buddha's closest disciples.
screen: `NAMES READ ONE AT A TIME.` → `GRIPPING THE CHAIR.` → `IS MY NAME ON THE LIST?`

segments.voice: Vyakarana is the Sanskrit word the Lotus uses for this kind of announcement: a prediction, a declaration, the Buddha saying out loud what someone's future will be. Sariputra received one in chapter three. Chapter six is named for it. The Buddha turns to Mahakasyapa, one of the disciples who told the story of the lost son, and declares that after honoring many Buddhas in ages to come, he will become a Buddha himself. Kern gives the name as Rasmiprabhasa, and the sutra describes his land: level, clean, with jeweled trees, free of rubble and thorns. Now the other great disciples, Subhuti, Katyayana and Maudgalyayana, are trembling. In Kern's translation they speak to the Buddha in verse, with a picture worth keeping. We are like a man who has come out of a famine, they say, and finds a royal meal set in front of him. He is starving, but he doesn't dare touch it until the king himself says: eat. They have heard that disciples can become Buddhas. They can't quite believe it applies to them until the Buddha says so by name. And the Buddha does. One by one he declares each a future Buddha, gives each a Buddha name, and describes each one's land and how long their teaching will last. The sutra takes its time over every one, as if no one should be hurried past. That is vyakarana in the Lotus. Not a horoscope about Tuesday. A teacher looking at a student and saying, in front of everyone: I see where you are going, and I am sure of it. The starving man is allowed to eat.
screen: `VYAKARANA: A DECLARATION.` · `KASYAPA WILL BE A BUDDHA.` · `A STARVING MAN AT A ROYAL MEAL.` · `EACH ONE NAMED.` · then, large: `A FUTURE FORETOLD.`

segments.voice: Is there someone waiting, quietly, to be told they'll be all right: a friend between jobs, a teenager, someone recovering? Silently wish them well about the road ahead, in a few plain words of your own, and hold the wish out the way you'd hold a meal out to someone hungry.
Vyakarana. A prediction or declaration: in the Lotus, the Buddha announcing that a disciple will become a Buddha, with a name and a land of their own. Today's word.
Your line: a future foretold. Like the king's word to a hungry man: eat. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: In Mahayana Buddhism a vyakarana is a Buddha's prediction that someone will reach Buddhahood; the Lotus Sutra gives a series of them, and some East Asian teachers read them as the one vehicle spoken to each hearer by name.

what it means: the Buddha's public declaration that a disciple will become a Buddha, with a name and a land.
what a scholar hears: the Lotus's chain of predictions, from Sariputra on, applies the one vehicle to named people; chapter six is titled for the vyakarana itself.

chat.says: When the Lotus Sutra 'predicts' a disciple's future, is that like a horoscope?
options: No. It's the Buddha declaring by name that a disciple will one day become a Buddha.
Yes. It tells each disciple what will happen to them in this life, day by day.
No. It's a warning that disciples who don't work harder will never be Buddhas.
chat.meaning: In chapter six, vyakarana is a declaration: the Buddha names each disciple's future as a Buddha, like a king telling a starving man to eat.
